FLA.body: Even though Florida may be without Barkov, the Panthers have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Sabres can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
paras: The Sabres won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-3 in Buffalo on Oct 12. The Sabres (9-9-4) beat Washington 6-3 on Thursday, while the Panthers (12-8-3) lost 5-2 to Edmonton on Tuesday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Sabres sixth (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Cats fifth (tied for 12th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 76-64, but only 46-43 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 23-13.

The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). The Panthers are the league’s most physical team: first in forecheck pressure, first in physicality and first in rough stuff. The Panthers’ power play (3rd) could do real damage against the Sabres’ penalty kill (25th). Beyond that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Tage Thompson (14 G / 10 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Florida. Jack Quinn (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 22 GP) is next in line. Matthew Tkachuk (7 G / 25 A / 32 P in 23 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, and Sam Reinhart (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.

Alex Lyon (0-2-1 / .898 SV% in 3 GS) is expected to start for Buffalo, and Jacob Markström (6-4-1 / .897 SV% in 12 GS) for Florida. Lyon has a .939 save percentage in six starts against the Panthers, well above his usual .901. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Paul Maurice likes to send Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Benson, Kulich and Thompson.
